plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels (a and b), each showing a diagram of a shallow neural network with one input node x, three hidden units h_1, h_2, h_3, and one output node y. In panel (a), two bias nodes labeled 1 are present — one feeding the hidden layer and one feeding the output — and the connections from hidden units to the output are labeled with weights φ_1, φ_2, φ_3 plus a bias weight φ_0; a single representative input-to-hidden weight θ_{11} is also labeled to indicate the notation convention. In panel (b), the weight labeling emphasizes the hidden-layer side: the bias connections to each hidden unit carry weights θ_{10}, θ_{20}, θ_{30}, and the connections from input x carry weights θ_{21} and θ_{31}, making the full first-layer parameterization explicit. Arrows in both panels use black and orange coloring to distinguish the input-side (pre-activation) connections from the output-side (post-activation) connections. This figure introduces the standard parameterization of a shallow network, showing how θ weights govern the input-to-hidden linear transformation and φ weights govern the hidden-to-output linear combination.

interactionPlan.concept: A shallow neural network computes output y by first using θ parameters to form hidden units h_i from the input x and bias, then using φ parameters to combine those hidden units into the final output.

demo_steps.title: Start with the architecture

interactionPlan.keyInsight: θ parameters build the hidden representations from x and bias, while φ parameters linearly combine those hidden representations to produce y.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a left-to-right neural network layout. In the clean view, show only x, the hidden units, y, and black directed arrows from x to hidden units and hidden units to y, with no weight labels or bias nodes unless a hidden unit is clicked. In the fully labeled view, include the two bias nodes labeled 1, orange bias arrows, θ labels on input-to-hidden and bias-to-hidden connections, φ labels on hidden-to-output and output-bias connections, and subtle teal highlights behind hidden units. When the hidden-unit count changes, keep x and y fixed horizontally while distributing h_i vertically; update labels systematically as θ_i0 for bias-to-hidden, θ_i1 for x-to-hidden, and φ_i for hidden-to-output.

discrepancies: The rendered figure is squeezed into the left portion of the page by the side UI, so the wide two-panel network appears far smaller than the source and does not fill the available canvas like the reference.
Most parameter labels, node labels, and panel labels are much smaller in the screenshot than in the source, making θ, φ, h_i, and even a)/b) hard to read at inline size.

The default narration says the viewer is in a clean architecture view, but the rendered default diagram and checkbox show the fully labeled parameter view, so the first demo step is semantically inconsistent.
The interactive slider can change the figure to 1–6 hidden units, which is conceptually reasonable but no longer matches the specific three-hidden-unit textbook figure unless reset.
